responses.evidence: B-03 now splits the failure shapes in both halves of the pair, and no gated observable asks the unedited #333 writer to append after a changed trailing event. Contract B-03 states up front that the writer takes no attemptId — it reloads state, acts on whatever rollbackableEvent returns (src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:1369-1390, predicate :1293-1302) and rechecks only the trailing event (:1412-1422) — so completion delegates only with a lineage it has just found still trailing this attempt's PENDING event, and enumerates three shapes: (a) precondition refusal (accepted-pair-invalid, lock-gate-refused) delegating with trigger deterministic-validation-refusal or lock-gate-refusal after that read; (b) a locked recheck lost only to scope-fingerprint drift with this attempt still trailing PENDING, delegating with the new trigger completion-cas-lost; (c) a trailing event that is no longer this attempt's PENDING event — a different attemptId, or this attemptId in another state — which appends nothing, restores nothing, calls no rollback and returns the module's existing refusal code facts-changed-before-lock (:133-134) naming both attemptIds. Shape (c) records the reason inline: delegating it is exactly what would roll back an attempt completion never admitted, because after ROLLED_BACK hasOpenRecoveryAttempt is false (:577-583) so a fresh PENDING attempt can be trailing and the writer would restore that attempt's snapshot and append for it; the alternative fix of teaching the writer an attemptId is refused as P-02-forbidden, and P-02 itself now names shape (c) as the consequence of pinning the writer. The PRD's restore-from-snapshot obligation is addressed rather than dropped: whatever moved the lineage past this attempt already ended it, or the 'Process death before completion commit' row hands it to #334's reconciliation. Manifest B-03 is restated per shape with those three givens and a per-shape observableResult, and the test plan's third bullet no longer targets the unreachable flavor: it now plants a ROLLED_BACK event for this attempt and a fresh PENDING event for a second attemptId (also via the beforeLockAcquired-style interleave seam) and asserts facts-changed-before-lock, an event-for-event unchanged lineage, byte-identical pair files and that the second attempt's snapshot is neither restored nor given an event. The fingerprint-drift bullet is stated separately as the only completion-cas-lost path.

B-01 no longer says 'before any write'. It now states the forbidden write concretely — completion 'appends no COMPLETED event and writes no run-state document of its own unless three preconditions hold' — names the code per precondition (accepted-pair-invalid for the pair, the new lock-gate-refused for a refusing gate and for a blank provenance, with the provenance grouped there as the lock exit's own stamp, recorded as a mechanical in-slice decision), and adds the terminal reading explicitly: 'A precondition refusal is terminal for the attempt, not a retryable non-write ... the attempt is then ended — it is not left PENDING — through B-03's delegation to #333's rollback writer, which restores the snapshot pair and appends ROLLED_BACK, or ROLLBACK_FAILED when the restore cannot be proven', with the one write-nothing exception pointed at B-03's changed-trailing-event shape. Manifest B-01's observableResult now asserts that ending, not only the code: per precondition it asserts the refusal code, that no COMPLETED event exists anywhere in the lineage, and that the trailing event afterwards is the ROLLED_BACK event rollBackRecoveryAttempt appended for the same attemptId, so no PENDING attempt remains — the retryable reading the finding said also passed now fails. The test plan's precondition bullet asserts the same thing, including the ROLLBACK_FAILED variant with an unreadable snapshot.
